owner: Journal, day 6, Sintra. Woke at 8:15. The weather was grey with a little drizzle. I spent the morning at a hillside vineyard and walked far more than I meant to, about 15,000 steps by the end of the day according to my watch. The streets here are steep and the pavements are those small polished stones that look lovely and are slippery when wet, so I took it slowly. I stopped twice for coffee and once just to sit on a wall and watch people go by. Around midday I got talking to Duarte, who runs a small shop near the square and has lived in Sintra all their life. Duarte told me I had to try the clam stew while I was here and wrote the name of a place on the back of my map. I went there in the evening and it was every bit as good as promised, a plain room with paper tablecloths and a television in the corner that nobody was watching. In the afternoon I did some washing in the sink, wrote two postcards, and tried to plan tomorrow without much success because the bus timetable on the wall of the station does not match the one online. I asked at the desk and was told, kindly, that neither is right and I should just turn up early. Money for the day: the room was 60 pounds, food came to 42 pounds altogether, and transport was 6 pounds, which makes 108 pounds for day 6. I am keeping an eye on that because the first week ran higher than I planned. Small things I want to remember: the smell of woodsmoke in the lane behind the guest house, a dog asleep in the doorway of the bakery, and the way the light came through the shutters at about six in the evening. My feet hurt, but in the good way. I also noticed my left boot is rubbing at the heel again, so I have put a plaster on it and will see how it is in the morning. Tomorrow I move on, and I want to be up early enough to see the market before the bus. One more note to myself: I keep meaning to ring home and keep forgetting until it is too late in the evening, so tomorrow I will do it at lunch. I should also back up the photos from the camera, because the card is nearly full and I would hate to lose the ones from a hillside vineyard. The guest house has a shelf of books other travellers left behind, and I swapped my finished paperback for a battered guide to the birds of the region, which I will probably never open but could not resist. Dinner tonight is the last of the bread and cheese from the market unless I find the energy to go back out. That is all for day 6. No need to comment on it, just say you have it.
